clue.text: Things people are going to say?

definitions.text: Things people are going to say?

parts.words: Things people are going to say?
parts.note: read cryptically, 'going' means departing, so these are the words said on leaving, not what people intend to say next

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about remarks someone is about to make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are going to say' reads as future intention; it really means what people say when they are going, that is leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Farewells are the words spoken by those departing, a fair cryptic description.

clue.text: Board work harmoniously

definitions.meaning: to board a bus or train is to climb aboard it
two people who work harmoniously have a friendly relationship

explanation.surface: Like a board of directors told to cooperate.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both mounting a vehicle and having a friendly rapport with someone.

clue.text: Players sit: boos break out

indicators.note: the letters break loose from their order and re-form, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Performers sit tight while booing erupts from the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' could mean actors or sportsmen, but 'break out' is the anagram signal on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboe players are instrumentalists, so they are players in an orchestra.

clue.text: No puritan, keen on American women?

parts.note: broad is US slang for a woman
minded means inclined or keen, as in 'minded to agree'

explanation.surface: A man who isn't prudish because he likes American women.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are written in the answer in the opposite order to the clue: the slang word for women comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A tolerant, liberal-thinking person is the opposite of a strict, prudish moralist.

clue.text: Crews have no head for heights

indicators.note: a word that has no head has lost its first letter, so heights is beheaded here

explanation.surface: Rowing crews are afraid of heights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have no head for' drops the first letter, H, from HEIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing boats with eight oarsmen, and their crews, are called by this number in rowing.

clue.text: London statue painful to put back

indicators.note: putting a word back here means writing it in the reverse direction

parts.note: sore means painful

explanation.surface: A London statue that would hurt to reinstall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses SORE. The statue stands at Piccadilly Circus in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged figure atop the Shaftesbury Memorial in Piccadilly Circus is popularly known by the Greek love god's name.

clue.text: One impaled on terrible horn — its?

definitions.text: One impaled on terrible horn — its?

indicators.note: a thing impaled on a spike is stuck right through, so one letter sits inside the jumble
terrible implies something mangled, so the word horn is jumbled

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A victim gored on a fearsome horn, and whose horn might it be?
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' scrambles HORN to RHNO, and 'impaled on' puts I inside it. The whole clue also describes the beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The horned animal whose horn has impaled someone is the large African or Asian pachyderm.

clue.text: Section of, say, people in street

indicators.note: the words before are placed in the middle of the street abbreviation

parts.note: eg (for example) is a stand-in for say
men means people, as in a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: A part of, for example, the people on a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is a crossword signal for an example abbreviation; 'in' is the container indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion or part divided off from a whole is a synonym.

clue.text: Persevering, even if difficult terrain

parts.note: tho is an informal spelling of though, meaning even if
rough going is hard ground to travel over

explanation.surface: Keeping on even though the ground is hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thorough and uncompromising carries a task through to the end, which is persistence.

clue.text: I obliged Ben to arrange feature of hotel room

indicators.note: arranging the letters means putting them in a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to set up something in a hotel bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to arrange' rearranges the eleven letters of I OBLIGED BEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A scripture volume placed by the Gideons in hotel bedrooms is a familiar fixture.

clue.text: Edged forward, with hooter?

definitions.meaning: a car or boat that edged forward moved slowly and carefully ahead
hooter is slang for the nose, so this means having a nose

explanation.surface: A car creeping forward and sounding its horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooter' looks like a car horn but is slang for a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is moving cautiously ahead; the adjective sense is possessing a nose, as in long-nosed.

clue.text: A little European larva

parts.note: a tad means a small amount
a Pole is a native of Poland

explanation.surface: A small European insect grub.
explanation.definitionFit: The aquatic young of a frog or toad is its larval stage.

clue.text: Profit from one number by country-and-western singer

indicators.note: by means beside, so the numeral and abbreviation sit next to the singer's surname, after it

parts.note: Johnny Cash was a famous country singer
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Making money from a single hit by a country star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' places I and N beside CASH, after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to exploit or take advantage of something for gain.

clue.text: Edges into study, bright red

indicators.note: the edges are put into the word for study

parts.note: to con is to study, an old verb
rims are edges

explanation.surface: Someone working at the borders of a vivid red design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' gives the old verb con, to learn by heart; 'into' is the container indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep, vivid shade of red is this colour.

clue.text: Compete to block drunkard in Russian council

indicators.note: blocking here means standing in the middle of the drunkard word, splitting it

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: Rivals try to keep a drunk out of a Russian assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'block' suggests keeping the drunkard out, but 'to block' is the container indicator, with the competing word sitting in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: In Russia and the USSR an elected governing assembly bore this name.

clue.text: President to refuse to allow a Japanese art form

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower
to ban is to forbid

explanation.surface: A president forbidding a Japanese art.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese art of flower arranging is the traditional craft meant.

clue.text: With power thrust forward and fall precipitously

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power
to lunge is to thrust forward, as in fencing

explanation.surface: Pushing forward forcefully and then tumbling steeply.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices or bodies that drop sharply and suddenly are said to do this.

clue.text: Popular, Castro, but no Christian

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Fidel Castro was the Cuban leader

explanation.surface: Castro was well-liked but not a believer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Castro' points to his first name, not the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbeliever, historically someone rejecting Christianity, is called this.

clue.text: Quickly grabbing uniform for opera

indicators.note: the speed word grabs the letter and holds it inside

parts.note: fast means quickly
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone hurriedly snatching a costume for the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Gounod's opera about the scholar who sells his soul has this title.

clue.text: Fit in curve round lake

indicators.note: the curve word goes round the lake abbreviation

parts.note: a bend is a curve
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Building a curving path around a lake so it fits.
explanation.definitionFit: To merge harmoniously with surroundings is to fit in.

clue.text: Avoid Santa Fe Trail city

definitions.meaning: to avoid is to sidestep or evade
... City in Kansas was a stop on the old Santa Fe Trail

explanation.surface: Steer clear of a frontier town.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means evade; Dodge City is the Kansas cow town on the old trail, known by its first word.

clue.text: Person consulted appearing uninterested in listening

parts.note: sounding means seeming or appearing, as in 'sounding keen'

indicators.note: in listening means as heard, so the word for uninterested is taken by its sound

parts.note: someone bored is uninterested

explanation.surface: A consultant who seems uninterested when hearing you out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in listening' turns BORED into the same-sounding BOARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose reactions are used to test out ideas is a confidant consulted informally.

clue.text: Crazy food for squirrel

explanation.surface: Mad about what squirrels eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for insane, and the hard-shelled seeds that squirrels gather.

clue.text: Drink beginning to befuddle Dame Edna

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken from befuddle

parts.note: Dame Edna Everage was Barry Humphries' comic character

explanation.surface: A drink that starts to make Dame Edna tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes B from befuddle. Dame Edna Everage was the Australian comic Barry Humphries' drag persona.
explanation.definitionFit: Any liquid for drinking is a general term for drink.
